note.en: Common mistakes and how to correct them: Mistaking the aortic arch branches for the pulmonary arteries. Correct it by following each branch back to the trunk, since arch branches never rejoin.

steps.en: What you see: The pulmonary trunk rises and splits into the right artery running under the aortic arch and the left artery climbing toward the lung. The bifurcation looks like an inverted Y on a good cranial tilt.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Tricuspid regurgitation peak velocity 2.8 m per s or less is normal.
Ductal flow is continuous through systole and diastole in a patent ductus.
Report the narrowest ductal diameter in millimetres with the gain set low.

Pitfalls: Lung air wipes out this view in adults with barrel chests, so try held breath out before giving up. A mirror artefact can double the trunk; a second vessel that moves exactly with the first is a mirror, not anatomy.

spot.en: Common mistakes and how to correct them: Mistaking the aortic arch branches for the pulmonary arteries. Correct it by following each branch back to the trunk, since arch branches never rejoin.
Oblique cut that fuses the two branches into one vessel. Correct it by tilting cranially until the division point is a sharp point rather than a blur.
Too basal a cut that loses the bifurcation. Correct it by sliding up one space and tilting toward the head again.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at left sternal edge, second intercostal space, cranial tilt.
Point the probe marker toward the left shoulder, about one o clock.
Sit high in the second space and tilt toward the head until the single trunk divides. In small children this is the window for ductal flow.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Check the ductal region in children.

why.en: Cranial tilt in a high space opens the division into both branches.

q.en: Colour bridges between trunk and aorta through the whole cycle in a neonate. What is this?

why.en: Continuous flow at the ductal site means a patent ductus in a neonate.

q.en: A second trunk moves exactly with the first. What is likeliest?

why.en: Exact synchronous motion marks a mirror artefact, not a second vessel.
